Every NRI living abroad knows this heartbreaking truth: We genuinely want to invest in our motherland’s growth story, but the Indian financial and regulatory system treats its own diaspora like untrusted outsiders, drowning us in a soul-crushing bureaucratic nightmare.
India proudly showcases UPI, DigiLocker, paperless governance, and missions to the Moon. Yet, the moment an NRI tries to invest hard-earned money into India, we are instantly shoved into a time machine back to 1985.
Look at the sheer absurdity of the process:
 * The Fragmented KYC Circus: Opening an NRE/NRO account is just circle one of Dante’s inferno. Once that is done, you want to invest in mutual funds? Surprise! Your bank KYC doesn't count. You must do KRA / Central KYC (CKYC) all over again. Nothing talks to each other. Every single intermediary operates in its own isolated silo.
 * The Attestation & Courier Puzzle: We are forced to print 40-page application dossiers, sign with wet ink, and hunt down Indian Embassies, Consulates, or overseas Notary Publics just for physical stamps. We take half-days off work, pay exorbitant attestation fees and notary commissions, and spend $50 to $100 per courier on DHL or FedEx—only to be told three weeks later that the application is rejected because "the notary stamp was placed on the wrong margin" or "the signature has a micro-variance."
 * The DTAA & Dividend Tax Nightmare: This is pure harassment. To avoid getting taxed at peak 20%+ TDS rates on dividends, NRIs must furnish Tax Residency Certificates (TRC) and Form 10F. Do you submit it once centrally? No! You have to manually track down and email/courier DTAA forms individually to every single bank, every single fund house, and every single listed company you hold shares in before their arbitrary record dates. If you hold 25 stocks, you are expected to correspond with 25 separate corporate secretarial desks every single financial year just to protect a few hundred rupees of dividend tax.
 * The Terrifying Data Privacy & Security Risk: While financial institutions preach compliance, their actual offline operational practice is reckless. Relationship managers, fund houses, and brokers casually instruct you: "Sir, please send self-attested copies of your passport, overseas visa, foreign utility bill, and bank statements over WhatsApp or unencrypted Gmail." These ultra-sensitive identity documents are forwarded aimlessly from customer care desks to backend processing units and compliance departments without audit trails or encryption. When identity theft happens, who takes responsibility?
 * Insurance & Demat Exploitation: The exact same exhausting friction repeats if you want a simple term insurance policy. On top of that, brokers slap punitive NRI Demat annual maintenance charges, specialized custodian fees, and non-PIS/PIS processing surcharges that domestic investors never have to face.
 * Punitive Tax Friction: Instead of welcoming remittances into wealth-generating assets, the tax regime hits NRIs with peak-slab withholding tax (TDS) upfront on LTCG, STCG, and dividends. We are forced to spend thousands more hiring Chartered Accountants to file cumbersome ITRs just to claim refunds on our legitimate, post-tax money.
Thousands of hours of productivity, endless sleepless nights tracking rejected tickets, and millions of dollars in courier and notary fees—all for what?
All of this can be solved with a single unified, secure digital portal: digital NRI KYC with passport chip verification, video-based KYC, digital Form 10F/TRC submission linked directly to PAN, and centralized DTAA tax relief.
NRIs aren't turning away from India because of lack of patriotism. We are walking away because the system exhausts our spirit. When an NRI can open a global brokerage account and invest in the US S&P 500 in less than 5 minutes on an app, why would anyone tolerate months of paper cuts, embassy lines, and WhatsApp document leaks for India?
If India truly wants diaspora capital to fuel its $5-10 Trillion economic ambitions, clean up this broken, fragmented bureaucracy. Digitize, centralize, and respect our time, our privacy, and our trust.

I think you need to understand a couple of things here. All these top company CEOs are saying good things about Indiamarket. just because they have to exit their investments at a good valuation. Imagine if they started pointing out the real issues: they would not be able to pull their investments out at a good profit. So, they say good things, and when the time is right, they just start exiting (which is already what FIIs are doing currently).

Now, there are two main things working against investing in India:

1. Rupee depreciation: for an FII, you do not invest in dollars, you invest in rupees. If the rupee is depreciating 5-7% per year, you have to factor that into your actual returns. If you are making an average of 8% long-term, but currency depreciation eats up 7%, your net return can even end up negative. Because of that, it makes very little sense for someone outside India to invest in the Indian market.
2. Long-term capital gains tax: it is currently and that also works directly against returns.

So, I really do not think you should take every public comment optimistically.
